metaData.title: When I Turned AI into an "Algorithm": The Engineering Journey of Skill Design
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into how Tencent engineers transformed an uncontrollable AI Agent into a precise, recoverable, and auditable deterministic component through a CLI execution layer, Workflow engine, and Gate mechanism.
metaData.summary: Centered on the core goal of "using Agent as an algorithm," this article systematically addresses two major pain points of LLMs in production: token waste and path uncertainty. The author proposes introducing a CLI program as a deterministic execution layer, shifting the Agent's role from a "free-willed entity" to a "decision engine" responsible only for understanding intent, collecting parameters, and organizing responses. All deterministic operations (API calls, format processing, state management) are handled by the CLI. The article details a three-layer tool management system (index layer, metadata layer, rule layer) to solve context explosion, along with core mechanisms of the Workflow engine such as step-by-step disclosure, Gate, state persistence, and template variables. It also demonstrates how to achieve systematic self-expansion through workflow-creator. The full text provides a complete engineering methodology from "writing prompts" to "building execution environments."
metaData.featuredReason: This article details an engineering philosophy to transform LLM Agents into precise, recoverable components. By treating Agents as "algorithms," the author proposes offloading deterministic tasks—like workflow sequencing, API calls, and state management—to a CLI. This "building a riverbed for AI" approach, leveraging step-by-step disclosure and file-based workflows, effectively mitigates LLM's probabilistic nature and memory limitations for scalable, reliable operations.

mainPoints.point: By introducing CLI as a deterministic execution layer, the uncertainty of the Agent is wrapped within a deterministic program.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent is only responsible for understanding intent and collecting parameters, while all API calls, format processing, and state management are handled by the CLI, fundamentally eliminating errors in precise operations.

mainPoints.point: The Workflow engine transforms open-ended problems into fill-in-the-blank tasks through step-by-step disclosure and Gate mechanisms.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent only sees the current step at any given moment. The Gate schema precisely defines completion criteria; stronger constraints reduce the Agent's cognitive load and improve execution reliability.

mainPoints.point: The state persistence mechanism enables the Agent to resume across sessions without relying on contextual memory.
mainPoints.explanation: The CLI writes process state to a JSON file on disk, allowing any session or model to resume from a checkpoint using --current, while also providing full auditability.

mainPoints.point: Workflow definitions are Markdown files on the file system, not code, enabling unlimited horizontal expansion of business capabilities.
mainPoints.explanation: Adding a new workflow only requires creating a new folder and step files in the workflows/ directory, with no code changes needed. Business users can define new processes simply by copying and pasting.

mainPoints.point: The system achieves self-bootstrapping through workflow-creator, allowing it to autonomously generate new capabilities.
mainPoints.explanation: Creating a new Workflow is itself a multi-step deterministic process. By engineering it through a second Skill, a closed loop of design, build, and execution is formed.

keyQuotes: Use the Agent as an algorithm. What does 'use it as an algorithm' mean? It means — you give it input, and it gives you output in a specified format. You don't care about the reasoning process in between, but the result is deterministic and predictable.
When it makes a mistake, we don't blame the model for lacking capability; instead, we think about what key factor is missing in the execution environment.

The stronger the constraints, the freer the AI becomes. When 'completion criteria' is a deterministic schema, the Agent's cognitive burden shifts from 'judging what counts as complete' to 'filling in these few fields.'
It's not about taming the AI, but building a riverbed it naturally flows through.

When you find yourself repeatedly writing 'be careful not to...' 'make sure to...' 'must...before...' in prompts — you are simulating a state machine with natural language. That is the signal to start engineering.
